chapter: Herbie Harper and Rasch's notes on Johnson
title: Ego, being a pacemaker and the Good Hearts
summary: He says you need some ego and should pave the way for the next guy, as he did with the Good Hearts and Crescendo Club.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Speaking of ego, I got a wonderful insight into J. C. the man when I asked him, "If you started to put your life together for a program, how would you want it to go?" He answered, "It's tough to do that yourself. There's got to be a certain amount of ego, and I always had to reach back and get a little bit of ego out of my back pocket to start up with the other guys."
Once -- another time we were talking about self worth and both of us working on it, and he said, "You've all got it up here. You've paved the way yourself. Be a pacemaker.
You fix it for the next guy. Let him follow you." And interestingly enough, this is what J. C. did do with the Good Hearts Welfare Association and the Crescendo Club.
